title: Gangu Shah Joins the Sikh Pilgrims and Offers a Humble Gift

blocks.text: This page introduces Gangu Shah as a poor hawker whose means are slight but whose hopes grow when he hears Sikhs speak about Guru Amar Das. Drawn by their testimony, he joins travelling Sikhs to Goindwal and begins moving from marketplace scarcity toward the possibility of grace.

On arriving, he is embarrassed by his poverty when he sees others offering gifts worthy of a great congregation. The page is careful to show that shame before the Guru can become either resentment or humility depending on how it is answered.
The Guru answers it generously by treating a small offering as meaningful. That is the opening condition from which both Gangu Shah's rise and his later corruption will unfold.
